subject: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp: EdgeWave proposal
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Ruiz <tanya@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp: EdgeWave proposal

Tanya — attaching a short set of dedicated reservation options based on our recent sizing workshop. High level, we scoped for your peak inference workload for the recommendation model and the chat assistant: ~55k daily active requests, ~2.5k concurrent users at peak, target p95 latency <= 120ms for 512-token responses.

Options (all include 99.5% availability SLA on Dedicated capacity and standard maintenance windows):

1) Lean / Proof-of-Value (low-risk)
- Cluster: 4x A100 80GB (reserved)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 2 (warm baseline)
- Planned ramp: 2-week onboarding -> steady state; ability to burst to 6 GPUs via shared burst pool for short peaks
- Typical throughput estimate: ~10–15 seq/s per GPU for your 2.1B quantized model
- Ideal if you want minimal up-front spend; will rely more on burst for short bursts

2) Standard (recommended)
- Cluster: 8x A100 80GB (reserved)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 4 (keeps latency headroom)
- Planned ramp: week 0–2: onboarding + perf tuning; week 3–6: gradual ramp to committed level; review checkpoints at week 2 and week 6
- Autoscale: Warm baseline (min 4), automatic ephemeral burst up to +50% during scheduled peak windows, with pre-warm triggers
- Throughput estimate: ~18–25 seq/s per GPU after tuning; targeted p95 <= 120ms for typical prompts

3) Performance / Peak (aggressive)
- Cluster: 16x A100 80GB (reserved) with 2 extra nodes for isolation (18 total)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 8
- Planned ramp: 6–8 week phased ramp with mandatory performance gate before each increment; includes pre-warmed burst pool and priority routing
- Recommended for buyers who require consistent sub-100ms p95 and zero degraded fallbacks

Commercial notes: all options come with an onboarding credit for the first 30 days (covers engineering ramp hours). We included rough monthly committed cost ranges in the attached PDF. We can also structure a staircase commitment (month 1: 50% commit, month 3: 100%) to soften cashflow.

Attachments: edgewave_dedicated_options_v1.pdf (proposal + cost ranges)

Next steps: pick an option + confirm target go-live window and any blackout dates you need us to avoid for maintenance. Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk the numbers.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tanya Ruiz <tanya@edgewave.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@edgewave.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp: EdgeWave proposal

Thanks Alex — the PDF looked good. A couple quick clarifying items before we present to procurement: 

1) Cost delta: can you give a ballpark percent delta between Standard and Performance (committed monthly cost)? We need that for the internal TCO slide.
2) Maintenance windows & regional failover: if you have a US region outage, can traffic failover to an EU Dedicated pool, or would that fall back to Hosted with different SLAs?
3) Contract term flexibility: is the staircase commit (50% -> 100%) offered only on 12m terms? Can we do a 6m pilot with a short-term commit and an option to extend?
4) During the ramp, what protections do we have for our critical trading-hour windows (we need guaranteed capacity 9:30–11:30 ET M–F)?

Also — would you be able to provide a short one-page risk/recovery note we can include with our security/compliance review (maintenance, patching cadence, pre-warm guarantees)?

If you can get answers by EOD Thursday, that would keep our internal timeline on track.

— Tanya
Tanya Ruiz
Head of Platform, EdgeWave
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp: EdgeWave proposal

Alex / Neha — quick internal note to align before we respond to Tanya. My recommendation: lead with the Standard option but bake in the following contractual and operational safeguards: 

- Guaranteed pre-warm window for trading hours (9:00–12:00 ET) where ephemeral burst capacity is reserved 24/7 for those times (explicit SLA objective). That can be modeled as a small additional monthly fee (we've used a +7% uplift historically).
- Staircase commit: offer a 6-month Pilot structure (committed minimum = 50% for months 1–2, 75% for months 3–4, 100% thereafter) as an alternative to a 12m staircase. This lowers procurement friction while protecting us on longer-term economics.
- Checkpoint gating: require usage-based ramp triggers (e.g., sustained 75% utilization across 72 hours) and formal sign-off at week 2 and week 6 for increasing the committed level. If performance regression shows p95 > 140ms we pause the ramp and allocate an optimization sprint.
- Failover behavior: during a regional outage, we prefer failing to Dedicated in another region (customer-managed VPC peering needed) but offer fallback to Hosted with degraded SLA if cross-region routing isn't possible. Spell this out in the SOW.
- Offering credit: provide a 10% ramp risk credit applied to the first 2 months of committed billing if we miss the initial performance gate. This reduces procurement resistance and aligns incentives.

I attached the internal ramp cost model we used to price the uplift by option (internal_ramp_costs_20261104.csv).

If Alex agrees, I'll draft the one-page risk/recovery note Tanya asked for and add the pilot staircase language.

— Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Ruiz <tanya@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp: EdgeWave proposal

Tanya — thanks for the quick questions and for the timeline. We've incorporated Dylan's recommendations and pulled together the answers below and an updated single-page appendix (attached) for your procurement/security packet. Summary: 

1) Cost delta: Standard -> Performance is ~+57% committed monthly cost at list for the same region (after accounting for reserved pricing). Exact dollar figures are in the attachment.
2) Maintenance & failover: We can offer cross-region Dedicated failover (US -> EU) but it requires a peering setup and an addendum in the SOW for cross-region data transfer and networking. If customer prefers not to peer, we fall back to Redwood Hosted with a degraded SLA (we'll document p95 increases and traffic routing behavior).
3) Contract flexibility: we will offer the 6-month Pilot staircase (50% -> 75% -> 100%) as requested. The pilot includes two formal checkpoint reviews and one performance optimization sprint included in the onboarding credit. Full 12m pricing with a 3% discount remains available if EdgeWave prefers longer term.
4) Trading-hour protection: we'll reserve an ephemeral pre-warm pool for 9:00–12:00 ET M–F. This is guaranteed in the SOW with an explicit uptime target for that window. Expected uplift +7% on committed spend to cover reservation of burst capacity.

Attached: updated_edgewave_appendix_onepager.pdf (risk/recovery + SLA summary), edgewave_dedicated_options_v1.pdf (updated cost table), DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/DS-78Y3K

If this looks good, please let me know which option you prefer (Lean / Standard / Performance) and whether you'll take the 6-month Pilot staircase or the 12-month commit. Once we have that, I'll route a clean SOW + DocuSign for signature and lock the onboarding calendar.

— Alex
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: updated_edgewave_appendix_onepager.pdf (one-page risk & SLA appendix)]
